statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail eases from 26 to 24, back inside the 20-24 watch band, while Stress rises to 85 in the extreme band.
recommendation: The extension sequence that carried Tail into the elevated band an hour ago has stopped. NQ has made no new low for a full hour, the 30,531.00 extreme is unbroken and price has recovered 43.50 points from it to 30,574.50, so the failed-retracement-plus-pinned-to-extreme structure is no longer observed. Fresh cross-asset evidence also withholds confirmation: the DAX is -0.05% and the Euro Stoxx 50 -0.15% against NQ at -1.02%, NVDA is only -0.36% pre-market despite SK Hynix falling 4.8% in Asia, and gold is down 3.14% rather than bid, which marks this as a rate-expectations repricing rather than a flight to safety. Tail therefore returns to 24 and the mapped policy state to WATCH. It is held at the top of the band, not lower, because three amplifiers are undiminished: the 10-year at 5.24% is at its highest since 2007, the VIX at 16.42 sits at its session high with no decay, and WTI is up 4.11% with Brent near 100.86 on an unresolved Strait of Hormuz standoff in which talks and strikes both remain possible. The unresolved AI-capex question left by the OpenAI training pause keeps a delayed second leg into the U.S. session credible, which is why the forecast returns Tail to the elevated band across the 13:00Z to 15:00Z window and why the danger window spans 13:00Z to 16:00Z. A fresh break of 30,531.00 that extends without a meaningful retracement would be the observation that carries Tail back above the watch band.
headline: NQ holds the 30,531.00 low for a full hour and recovers 43.50 points to 30,574.50 at -1.02%; a near-flat DAX, NVDA only -0.36% pre-market and gold -3.14% withhold confirmation, easing Tail to 24 and the state to WATCH while Stress rises to 85
body:
Nasdaq-100 futures trade at 30,574.50 on the 10:16Z Yahoo Finance quote and 30,575.00 on the 10:15Z Investing.com quote, 314.75 and 314.25 points or 1.02% below Friday's 30,889.25 settlement. Both feeds report an unchanged session low of 30,531.00, the same extreme that was current at the previous assessment, and Yahoo Finance puts the Globex high at 30,920.75 for a 389.75-point range. Investing.com's narrower calendar-day range of 30,531.00 to 30,705.50 places the current price in the lower third of today's trade rather than at its extreme.

The decisive change since the previous hour is that the extension sequence has stopped. An hour ago price had failed a 57-point bounce, extended to a fifth successive Globex lower low and was pinned within 18 points of it, which is why Tail crossed into the elevated band at 26. Over the following hour no new low was made and price has recovered 43.50 points off 30,531.00. Repeated extension after a failed retracement is the observed structure the Tail score exists to flag, and for this hour it is no longer present. Tail therefore returns to 24 at the top of the watch band and the mapped policy state becomes WATCH.

Fresh cross-asset evidence withholds the confirmation a persistent one-way path would require. European cash indices are close to unchanged, with the DAX at 25,394.79 or -0.05% and the Euro Stoxx 50 at 6,293.52 or -0.15%, both on 10:11Z to 10:13Z quotes, while NQ is down 1.02%. Inside the Nasdaq-100 itself the transmission is narrow rather than broad: NVDA is quoted at 224.25 pre-market, only -0.36% against its 225.07 close, even though SK Hynix fell 4.8% and Samsung Electronics 4.6% in Asia. ASML's U.S. listing is weaker at 1,714.08 or -1.71%. Gold is the clearest tell, down 3.14% to 4,185.60 from 4,321.20: a decline in gold alongside falling equities and rising yields identifies a real-rate and rate-expectations repricing rather than a flight to safety, and that class of move has historically produced two-sided, retracing equity paths.

The amplifier set nevertheless remains intact, which is why Tail sits at the top of the watch band rather than lower. The U.S. 10-year yield is 5.24%, up about 7 basis points and at its highest since 2007, with the 2-year at 4.93%, the 5-year at 5.07% and the 30-year at 5.54%. The VIX is 16.42, up 10.43% from Friday's 14.87 close, and its day range of 16.10 to 16.42 means the volatility bid is at its high for the session with no intraday decay. WTI is 96.23, up 4.11%, and Brent is 100.86 on the direct futures feed, up 3.51% within a 97.63 to 101.06 range. One aggregator quoted Brent materially higher at 108.43; that single outlier is treated as a data inconsistency rather than a price, since the direct futures quote and the WTI level agree with each other.

Two catalysts drive the backdrop and both are two-sided. OpenAI has paused training, evaluation and inference with tool use for its most capable models pending a safety review, which reopened the question of whether the pace of AI investment in chips, servers and data centres can slow. That question is unresolved, and it is the reason a delayed second leg into the U.S. cash session remains credible. On Iran, President Trump rejected Tehran's seven-day proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz on 26 September, but talks are expected to resume this week and he declined to commit either way on strikes before the November midterms, while Iran's foreign minister said Tehran remains ready for both diplomacy and renewed conflict. A catalyst that can resolve in either direction raises the volatility environment measured by Stress and the event-path uncertainty in the published forecast, and it does not by itself establish the directional efficiency that Tail measures.

Stress rises to 85 in the extreme band. Oil is up more than 4% on WTI, the 10-year is at a 19-year high and still rising, gold has lost more than 3%, the VIX has gained over 10% and the week ahead carries ADP, Core PCE and final Q2 GDP on Wednesday, ISM Manufacturing on Thursday and Non-Farm Payrolls on Friday, with quarter-end rebalancing on 30 September. That is a genuinely difficult, high-volatility environment in which a large but recoverable drawdown is plausible, and it can coexist with Tail below the blocking threshold. Confidence is 86: two independent NQ feeds agree on price, change and the session low, the full yield curve, VIX, gold, WTI and Brent are current, two European indices and two U.S. pre-market single names are live, and both catalysts are verified against primary reporting. Confidence is held below 90 because of the single conflicting Brent print and because the shared Finviz context was 267 minutes old with its futures and calendar sections unavailable, so it contributed nothing to this assessment.

The published danger window is 13:00Z to 16:00Z, covering the 13:30Z cash open, the post-open continuation window and the 14:30Z Dallas Fed Manufacturing release. That is where an aligned opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks would represent the observed evidence needed to carry Tail back into the elevated band. A fresh break of 30,531.00 that extends without a meaningful retracement, or a European close that finally confirms the overnight direction, would be the invalidations of the present reading.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry published Claude assessments. Tail held at 7-8% through the Sunday European and U.S. hours, drifted from 9% to 14% across the Globex reopen as Stress climbed from 63% to 76%, eased to 9-12% between 00:00Z and 02:00Z, then stepped to 21% at 03:00Z when NQ first took out Friday's low, 22% at 04:00Z, 21% at 05:00Z and 24% for the three hours from 06:00Z to 08:00Z as successive overnight lows broke, before crossing to 26% at 09:00Z on a failed retracement. Stress rose almost monotonically from 63% to 84% and Confidence from 69% to 85%. Dominant mode was normal for seventeen hours, mixed at 02:00Z and 05:00Z and trend-down at 03:00Z, 04:00Z and for the four hours from 06:00Z to 09:00Z. Seventeen hours mapped to EA_ON, six to WATCH and the most recent one to BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES.
outlookSummary: The published horizon runs from the 10:00Z hour on 28 September through 09:00Z on 29 September. Tail opens at 24% at the top of the watch band and enters the 25-34 elevated band for only three hours, 13:00Z to 15:00Z, peaking at 28% on the 14:00Z hour that covers post-open continuation risk and the 14:30Z Dallas Fed Manufacturing release. It returns to the watch band from 16:00Z, drifts between 21% and 24% through the Asian session with a local high of 24% on the 01:00Z hour when China and Korea reprice the AI-capex question for a second session, and falls to 18% in the low band only for the 21:00Z CME maintenance halt, when no meaningful price discovery exists. Stress holds between 80% and 86% throughout, reflecting WTI up 4.11%, a 10-year yield at its highest since 2007, gold down 3.14% and a week carrying ADP, Core PCE and final Q2 GDP on Wednesday, ISM Manufacturing on Thursday and Non-Farm Payrolls on Friday alongside quarter-end rebalancing. Confidence decays from 86% to 62% with distance from the evidence cutoff. Every hour beyond the current one states its structure conditionally, as a checkpoint, assumption or invalidation.

An aligned opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks is the specific structure this score exists to flag. The counterweight already on record is that NVDA is only -0.36% pre-market, so the Asian chip selloff has not yet transmitted to the largest Nasdaq-100 semiconductor.
